note: Attacker-controlled raw input bytes are written to a temporary .pcap file for parsing
The .pcap file is read and the first packet is extracted as a RawPacket
The raw packet is parsed into protocol layers; a DHCP packet with truncated options is identified
For DHCP packets, getOptionsCount() is called which invokes getTLVRecordCount() on the options area
getTLVRecordCount calls getFirstTLVRecord with the DHCP options pointer and options length (0 bytes for truncated packet)
A DhcpOption TLVRecord is constructed with the pointer to the options area; no bounds check is performed on tlvDataLen
getTotalSize() is called on the DhcpOption which reads m_Data->recordType and m_Data->recordLen from the options buffer without verifying tlvDataLen is sufficient
Reads recordType (1 byte at offset 0) from the options buffer which is 0 bytes long, causing an out-of-bounds read past the heap buffer

Reads recordLen (1 byte at offset 1) from the options buffer which is 0 bytes long; the compiler may combine recordType and recordLen reads into a single wider access, resulting in a heap-buffer-overflow READ 4
The out-of-bounds read in getTotalSize() occurs before the bounds check can reject the record, triggering the heap-buffer-overflow in the vulnerable code
